items.abstract: <jats:p>Molecular property prediction and chemical reaction analysis are fundamental tasks in computational chemistry with critical applications in drug discovery and materials design. While large pre-trained molecular models have achieved remarkable performance, their computational cost severely limits deployment in resource-constrained environments. Moreover, existing methods struggle with cross-domain knowledge transfer, multi-task learning for diverse molecular endpoints, and the integration of spectral data with molecular graph representations. In this paper, we propose ChemDistill, a unified framework for chemical knowledge distillation with hierarchical graph attention that addresses these challenges through three complementary modules. First, the Hierarchical Graph Attention Distillation module transfers knowledge from large teacher models to lightweight student models through flow-based distillation with a calibration mechanism that corrects systematic biases inherited from the teacher. Second, the Chemistry-specific Parameter-Efficient Multi-Task Adapter enables simultaneous prediction of multiple molecular properties with only ten percent of full fine-tuning parameters through task-shared and task-specific adapter components. Third, the Spectrum-Molecular Joint Representation module fuses spectral data including infrared spectroscopy and nuclear magnetic resonance with molecular graph features via cross-modal attention, enabling end-to-end prediction from raw spectral inputs to molecular properties. Extensive experiments on MoleculeNet, QM9, and USPTO benchmarks demonstrate that ChemDistill achieves state-of-the-art performance across all tasks while requiring only 1.6 million parameters, approximately a 3.3 times compression ratio compared to the teacher model. On the Tox21 benchmark, ChemDistill achieves a ROCAUC of 0.879, outperforming the teacher model ChemBERTa while being significantly more compact. For chemical reaction prediction on USPTO, ChemDistill attains a Top-1 accuracy of 51.6 percent, surpassing existing methods by a substantial margin. Keyword: Knowledge Distillation, Molecular Property Prediction, Graph Neural Network, Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning, Spectral Analysis</jats:p>
title: ChemDistill: Hierarchical Graph Attention Distillation with Parameter-Efficient Multi-Task Adapters for Molecular Property Prediction and Chemical Reaction Analysis

items.abstract: <jats:p>The proliferation of large language models with billions of parameters has rendered full finetuning computationally prohibitive for most downstream applications, catalyzing intensive research into parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods. Traditional adapter layersbottleneck modules inserted within transformer blocks-have emerged as a foundational approach, enabling task-specific adaptation by training fewer than 1% of model parameters. However, these methods exhibit significant limitations in data-scarce scenarios, requiring substantial task-specific examples to achieve competitive performance. This paper presents a comprehensive comparative analysis of Meta-Adapters, a meta-learning enhanced variant, against traditional adapter architectures including Houlsby adapters, LoRA, and AdaLoRA. We systematically examine their architectural foundations, parameter efficiency, computational characteristics, and empirical performance across single-task, few-shot, multi-task, and multilingual learning settings. The analysis demonstrates that Meta-Adapters achieve competitive few-shot accuracy-improving by large margins over traditional adapters while finetuning only 0.6% of parameters-and perform comparably to GPT-3 with models 1,590× smaller. We further explore emerging tensor-based adapters including MetaTT and MeTA-LoRA, which extend meta-learning principles through tensor train decompositions and two-stage optimization frameworks. Our findings reveal that the integration of meta-learning with adapter architectures fundamentally addresses the data efficiency limitations of traditional approaches, establishing a new paradigm for parameter-efficient few-shot learning. We conclude by identifying open challenges and promising directions for future research in meta-learned adapter systems.</jats:p>
title: A Comparative Analysis of Meta-Adapters and Traditional Adapter Layers for Parameter-Efficient Learning

items.abstract: <jats:p>Molecular representation learning is essential for computational chemistry, yet existing methods struggle with multi-modal inputs and costly fine-tuning. We propose ChemMamba, a unified framework integrating multi-modal diffusion pre-training with parameter-efficient chemical adapters. Our approach features a cross-modal encoder that aligns SMILES strings, 2D graphs, and 3D conformations via a diffusion-based objective, capturing complementary structural and geometric features. To address the high cost of model adaptation, we introduce Chem-Adapters, which enable multi-task transfer learning with only 1.6M trainable parameters, a 53× reduction compared to full fine-tuning. Furthermore, a linear-attention diffusion generator is incorporated to reduce the computational complexity of molecular generation from quadratic to linear. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets (MUV, Tox21, SIDER, and ClinTox) demonstrate that ChemMamba achieves state-of-the-art results in property prediction, specifically reaching an AUROC of 0.841 on MUV and 0.908 on ClinTox. In molecular generation tasks on ZINC250K, Chem-Mamba achieves a validity score of 0.952 and a Fréchet ChemNet Distance (FCD) of 8.47, significantly outperforming existing diffusion-based baselines. These results highlight the efficiency and robustness of ChemMamba for both discriminative and generative tasks in drug discovery.</jats:p>
title: ChemMamba: Multi-Modal Diffusion Pre-Training with Parameter-Efficient Adapters for Molecular Property Prediction and Generation
